sections.h2: Which Guilford County offices value property and take payment?
sections.html:
Guilford County's Tax Department sets values and mails bills, and walk-in help comes from two buildings: 400 W. Market St. in Greensboro and 325 E. Russell Ave. in High Point. Doors are open weekdays from 8 in the morning until 5 in the afternoon.

Guilford dates to 1771 and has a courthouse in each of its two big cities. The state encyclopedia says the seat moved to Greensboro in 1808. Census Bureau estimates credit the county with 562,234 people in mid-2025 on 645.92 square miles of land, so a listing might be a High Point bungalow or acreage near Summerfield.

Payment channels the department lists:

  • The Pay It portal, online or at (336) 203-7795, adds a 1.85% electronic fee and a $2 transaction fee.
  • Checks go to P.O. Box 70939, Charlotte, NC 28272-0939, payable to Guilford County Tax Department.
  • Counter payments accept cash, checks and cards, and card payers add 2.35% plus $2. Gift cards cannot be used.

sections.h2: How did the 2026 reappraisal and moratorium affect Guilford bills?
sections.html:
Bills for 2026 carried 2025 values, so the reappraisal numbers debut on the 2027 bill. Senate Bill 889 put a one-year hold on the reappraisal that began January 1, 2026, and the county confirms that Guilford is covered.

State revenue officials told Guilford in April 2023 to reappraise because most parcels were selling above their assessed values. Staff appraisers did the work themselves, and owners received notices in February 2026. The county lists 2032 as the following reappraisal year.

An owner who had already appealed the 2026 value keeps that appeal alive, according to the county, and it carries to the next bill. Commissioners set the fiscal year 2026-27 rate at 78.95 cents per $100, which is 5.9 cents higher than before. The rate went up in 2026 while the new values arrive in 2027, so the two changes land in different years.

sections.h2: When do Guilford County tax bills come due, and when does interest begin?
sections.html:
The bill is payable September 1 under state law and carries no interest through January 5. Guilford's FAQ agrees with the January 5 cutoff and expects bills in the first half of July.

Paying early earns a discount. The FAQ prints 0.5% for payment by August 31, while the county's moratorium notice said payers who beat Monday, August 31, 2026 would still get 1%. Ask the Tax Department which figure fits your bill.

After the cutoff, interest starts at 2% for month one and 0.75% per month beyond that. The county says collection steps begin immediately: garnishment of wages and bank accounts, levies on personal property, attachment of state refunds and lottery prizes, and eventually foreclosure. It adds that it holds no tax lien sales.

Mailed payments are timed by postmark. Without a Postal Service postmark, the day the office receives the envelope counts, and the taxpayer must prove it was on time.

sections.h2: How does a Guilford County owner dispute an assessment?
sections.html:
Send a written appeal to the Board of Equalization and Review between January 1 and May 15. The 5 p.m. cutoff moves to the following working day when May 15 lands on a weekend or holiday. The county accepts online filings, and the paper form is available from 336-641-4814.

Under the moratorium law, the board's page keeps 2026 appeals open through December 31, 2026 and lets 2027 appeals run to May 17, 2027. The online portal reopens January 1, 2027, and taxreval@guilfordcountync.gov can mail a form earlier.

An appraiser reviews the file and makes a recommendation. If you agree, the matter ends. If not, you get a hearing date before the five-member board, where the county value is presumed right and the owner must supply proof. Guilford lists useful proof:

  • Closed sales of comparable homes near the reappraisal date, last year's appraisal, or a contractor quote that puts a number on a defect.
  • Errors in square footage or on the property record card, and outside influences such as a flood zone.

Taxpayers cannot win on the size of the increase or on trouble paying, and forced sales do not qualify as comparables. A written decision comes in about two weeks. An owner who still disagrees may take the case to the state Property Tax Commission by filing notice within 30 days of the board's mailing.

sections.h2: Which Guilford County relief programs reduce what a homeowner owes?
sections.html:
Three programs are available, and one benefit per owner is the limit. Applications are due June 1, and later ones go before the Board of Equalization and Review if complete at least a week before its last December meeting.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: removes the larger of $25,000 or half the home's value from taxation. Qualifying owners are 65 or totally and permanently disabled on January 1, and gross income cannot pass $38,800 on the county's page. It needs one application.
  • Circuit breaker: caps the yearly bill at 4% of income, or 5% when income falls between $38,800 and $58,200. Five years of owning and living in the home are required, and the owner reapplies annually.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: removes the first $45,000 of value regardless of age or income, for a veteran with a total and permanent service-connected disability or an unmarried surviving spouse.

Sellers should look hardest at the circuit breaker. The tax above the cap is deferred and sits as a lien, and when the home transfers, the most recent three years of deferred tax become payable with interest. The exclusions carry no repayment. Mail applications to PO Box 3138, Greensboro, NC 27402, or deliver them to either tax office. Call 336-641-3320 or 336-641-7911 with questions.

sections.h2: What should a Guilford seller do about a tax balance?
sections.html:
Clear it at or before closing. North Carolina attaches the lien to a parcel on its January 1 listing date, interest and penalties included, which means a buyer's title search surfaces it.

With an escrow account, the servicer asks the county for the bill and you receive a notice around mid or late July, per the Tax Department. The notice leaves the legal duty with you, so confirm the amount was paid. Without escrow, pay directly before interest starts.

If taxes stay unpaid, the county may foreclose in court in a proceeding patterned on a mortgage foreclosure, ending with an auction at the courthouse door and a ten-day window for higher bids after the commissioner reports the sale. Selling first keeps the price with you. The Tax Department's bill search shows the payoff, and our register of deeds guide explains how the deed records afterward.

Items worth checking before listing a Guilford house:

  • A circuit breaker deferral that comes due on transfer.
  • A parcel record that no longer matches the house after an addition. An online Property Verification form fixes this, and the county says the record card updates in about 48 hours.
  • Vehicle gap bills, which arrive separately from the real estate bill.

sections.h2: What does the Census say about housing in Guilford County?
sections.html:
QuickFacts puts Guilford's housing stock at 246,403 units and says owners live in 59.9% of occupied homes. A typical home that its owner lives in is valued at $259,900 on the 2020 to 2024 survey. Monthly owner costs run $1,536 with a mortgage and $515 without, and rent has a middle of $1,163.

Household income centers on $68,642 in 2024 dollars. The county issued 2,876 building permits in 2025, and 18.0% of residents are 65 or older, the group the relief programs target.

faqs.q: Were Guilford's 2026 tax bills based on the new reappraisal?
faqs.a: No, they used 2025 values because Senate Bill 889 paused the reappraisal for a year. The new values apply to the 2027 bill, appeals filed against them are still processed, and the county lists 2032 as the next reappraisal.

faqs.q: What is the last day to file a Guilford County value appeal?
faqs.a: May 15 at 5 p.m. in a normal year, with the appeal received or postmarked by then. The moratorium law extended 2026 appeals to December 31, 2026 and set May 17, 2027 for 2027 appeals, per the board's page.

faqs.q: Can seniors or veterans pay less property tax in Guilford County?
faqs.a: Yes. An owner who is 65 or older or totally disabled and under the income cap can exclude the larger of $25,000 or half the home's value, and a qualifying disabled veteran can exclude $45,000. File with the Tax Department by June 1.

faqs.q: What becomes due if a circuit breaker owner sells?
faqs.a: The most recent three years of deferred tax, with interest, come due on the transfer date. A sale is a disqualifying event under the program, so request a payoff figure from the Tax Department before closing.

faqs.q: How can I pay the Guilford County tax bill?
faqs.a: Use the Pay It portal online or by phone, mail a check to the Charlotte post office box on the bill, or pay at the Greensboro or High Point office. Card payments carry a fee, and gift cards are refused.
